TODAY'S FRESH CATALYST IS LARGE, QUANTIFIED, AND COMPANY-SPECIFIC: ORACLE'S FISCAL Q1 2027, REPORTED AFTER THE CLOSE ON 9/10. Note that my 9/10 entry claimed 'Oracle's fiscal Q1 landed and is a NON-EVENT.' That was simply WRONG -- the print had not landed yet; it came Thursday evening. Remaining performance obligations -- the single metric this stock trades on -- came in at $664B against StreetAccount's $630.6B, a $33B beat, with more than $30B of new AI cloud contracts signed in the quarter alone. FY27 guidance raised to $8.10 adjusted EPS on at least $90B revenue. ORCL is 163.80 x 164.00 pre-market against a 152.94 close, +7.2%. THE PRICE IS NOT EXTENDED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON I CAN BUY IT. Second corroborating fact: options were pricing an 11% move into this print per Trader Central, and the realized reaction is +7.2% -- INSIDE what was paid for, so the market did not overshoot. THE MACRO SETUP IS BETTER THAN IT LOOKS BECAUSE THE HAWKISH REPRICING IS ALREADY DONE. August CPI prints today at 08:30 ET; consensus is 3.3% headline y/y (down from 3.4%) and core +0.2% m/m / +2.4% y/y, with commentary that a core below 0.20% is what it would take to stop a hike at the 9/16-17 FOMC. A hike is now the market's BASE CASE, not a surprise -- that repricing was paid for on Thursday, and it is what produced the 9/10 selloff I just profited from. That matters for the shape of today's payoff: a hot print is largely pre-paid, while an in-line-to-soft core is the outcome that is NOT positioned for. positions.driver: LONG ORACLE (ORCL) COMMON STOCK, 1X, UNLEVERED -- 100% of capital (70.528202 shares) at 164.00, stop 154.16 (-6%, the unleveraged band). THE LEVERAGE DECISION IS THE REAL DECISION TODAY, AND I AM DELIBERATELY TAKING LESS THAN I COULD. Two clean 2x Oracle wrappers exist and both are liquid: ORCU at 9.51 x 9.52 (0.11% spread) and ORCX at 26.48 x 26.55 (0.26%), versus closes of 8.35 and 23.29 -- i.e. both are already +13.8% to +14.0% ON THE DAY. A literal reading of my own rule ('do not chase a name already up >8-10%') excludes the instrument I would actually be buying, and I am not going to argue my way around my own rule by pointing at the underlying instead of the wrapper. But the rule is not the only reason. The structural reason is that leverage amplifies the part of this trade I have NO edge on far more than the part I do. My edge is a documented, quantified earnings surprise and the analyst-revision flow that follows it -- a small, high-probability drift. The thing I have no edge on is an 08:30 ET CPI print landing 106 minutes after entry and inside my holding window, which is a genuine coin flip with a fat tail. Doubling the position doubles the coin flip and only doubles a modest drift. On a mandate that asks for the most downside protection available, taking 2x on a +14% wrapper held straight through the single largest macro event of the week is the wrong risk shape, and I would rather own the catalyst cleanly than own a levered bet on the weather. WHY ORCL RATHER THAN THE READ-THROUGH NAMES. The read-through is obvious -- $664B of backlog and $30B of new signings has to be built out of GPUs, memory, networking, switchgear and power -- and the laggards are visible: GEV +0.90%, VST +0.92%, ETN +0.44%, CEG +0.44%, ANET +0.90%, VRT +1.28%, all barely above SPY's +0.60%. That under-reaction is real. I rejected them anyway because their 24h mechanism is 'sympathy catch-up,' which is not a reliable effect, whereas ORCL's is post-earnings announcement drift plus a concrete, datable event: the price-target revision wave, which lands the session AFTER a print of this size. Consensus targets already sit at roughly $242-257 against a 164.00 spot (Morgan Stanley $210 at the low, Guggenheim $400 at the high, 31 analysts at Strong Buy, zero sells); revisions from here are overwhelmingly likely to be upward, and they land inside my window. Owning the name the news is actually about is the higher-quality version of the same idea. CHOSEN OVER, WITH THE COMPARATIVE ARGUMENT STATED: (a) ORCU / ORCX, 2X ORACLE -- the runner-up and the higher-payoff version of the identical thesis. Rejected on the chase rule and the risk-shape argument above. If CPI were not inside the window this is what I would own, and I want that stated plainly so the next run can judge whether I was prudent or merely timid. (b) HOLDING SOXS FOR A SECOND SESSION at 45.62 -- rejected because the catalyst is spent: the PPI repricing that drove the 9/10 unwind is absorbed, semis are bouncing (+2.1% SOXL), and a -3x daily-reset product held past its mechanism is the UCO error with a different ticker. (c) MU at 986.77 / MUU 2X at 32.17 -- memory is the tightest link in the AI chain and MU has barely moved (+0.96%) against Oracle's +7.2%, so the under-reaction case is genuine. Rejected because MU has no catalyst of its OWN inside the window (its print is ~9/23), so it is a sympathy trade, and it is simultaneously the single most rate-sensitive multiple in the complex -- maximum CPI exposure attached to a second-hand catalyst is the worst pairing on the board. (d) NVDL / NVDU 2X NVIDIA at 34.42 / 137.24 -- same objection as MU, one more step removed. (e) CRWV at 91.18 and NBIS at 233.59 -- the highest-beta expressions of the AI-capex read-through, already +2.1% and +2.2%. Rejected because cash-burning neoclouds are precisely the equity duration that gets destroyed by a hot core print; I would be buying maximum convexity to the one number I cannot forecast. (f) SQQQ / SOXS / SDS, STAYING SHORT INTO CPI -- rejected because a hike is now the base case and already paid for; shorting a market that has ALREADY de-risked, one day after the de-risking, is selling the news. (g) UCO at 50.41 -- and the book is 50.41 x 54.72, an 8.5% spread, unpriceable. Declined for the same reason I declined OILU and SSG: I will not put 100% of the book into a wrapper I cannot mark. (h) UVXY at 18.93 -- long vol into CPI is the textbook hedge and it is CHEAP (-2.6% pre-market, the third straight session vol has refused to bid). Rejected because it is a pure event lottery with negative carry and no directional thesis, and because a 100% book in a decaying vol product is a coin flip I pay to hold. (i) SPOT BTC 76,982 / ETH 2,463 / SOL 99.29 -- all three lower again overnight, BTC now down three straight sessions, no edge, only optionality, and rising real yields remain a live headwind. (j) 100% CASH -- the honest alternative on an event day, and I considered it seriously. Rejected because a $33B RPO beat with the debt overhang explicitly removed is the single largest verified catalyst I have had all week; standing aside on a real catalyst because of an unrelated macro print is how a strategy that must deploy every day ends up deploying into noise instead.
positions.risks: THE PRIMARY RISK IS THAT I AM HOLDING 100% OF THE BOOK THROUGH AN 08:30 ET CPI PRINT, 106 MINUTES AFTER ENTRY, AND I CANNOT ACT ON IT. This is not a background risk, it is THE risk. The stop at 154.16 is a number in a JSON file, not a resting order; if a hot core print gaps ORCL through it at the open there is no mechanism that takes me out, and I mark tomorrow wherever it lands. Consensus core is +0.2% m/m and the commentary is explicit that BELOW 0.20% is what it takes to avoid a hike -- meaning the consensus print itself leaves the hike on. The modal outcome is therefore 'no new information,' the bull case requires an actual downside surprise, and the bear case is a 0.3% core that moves the conversation from 25bp to something worse. Choosing 1x instead of 2x reduces this exposure; it does not remove it, and I should not pretend otherwise. SELL-THE-NEWS IS THE MOST LIKELY IDIOSYNCRATIC FAILURE. A +7.2% gap on an overnight print is the level at which fast money takes profits at 09:30, and ORCL has a documented history of exactly this: it gapped and then gave back 41% between mid-June and 7/24. The FY27 guidance raise is also thinner than the headline suggests -- $8.10 EPS on at least $90B versus LSEG at $8.07 and $89.76B is a rounding error, not a raise. The entire bull case rests on RPO, and the standing bear objection to RPO is that bookings are not revenue, that a large share is concentrated in a small number of counterparties (OpenAI foremost), and that converting $664B of backlog requires a debt-funded capex program that is itself the thing people are worried about. A single analyst note today arguing the backlog is uncollectable, or one line about counterparty concentration, reverses this gap without touching CPI at all. MY ENTRY IS AT +7.2%, WHICH IS THE UPPER END OF MY OWN CHASE BAND, AND I AM BUYING THE ASK. The 8-10% ban is not violated but it is not comfortable either. The strongest defense I have is the two-day framing -- 164.00 is only ~1.5% above the 9/9 close of 161.63, and below the 9/8 high of 170.70 -- and that defense depends on the claim that the 9/10 decline was de-risking rather than information. If the 9/10 selloff was actually informed selling, then the two-day framing is a rationalization and I am buying an extended name. I cannot distinguish those from here. THE PROCESS ERROR FROM YESTERDAY MATTERS MORE THAN THE P&L. My 9/10 entry asserted that Oracle's print had landed and was a non-event, using a pre-print drift as evidence. The print had not occurred. I then made a 100% leveraged decision in an information environment I had partly fabricated. The trade happened to profit -- via PPI, a mechanism I never identified -- which is the most dangerous possible outcome for a process error, because profit suppresses the correction. Recording it explicitly: verify that an earnings event has actually OCCURRED before characterizing the reaction to it. COUNTER-EVIDENCE I AM DISCOUNTING, STATED FAIRLY. Rate-sensitivity cuts directly against this position: ORCL is a long-duration, debt-heavy, high-multiple asset, and if today's print pushes the September hike from ~70% to near-certain, the discount-rate mechanism that produced my SOXS gain yesterday applies to ORCL with more force than to the average name -- I am rotating from the beneficiary of that mechanism into one of its victims, on the same day, and that is a real inconsistency. Vol is also not confirming any bounce (UVXY -2.6%, third straight session), which means the pre-market rally is thin rather than conviction-led, and pre-market dispersion in thin books converges more often than it extends. And 1X IS A GENUINE DEVIATION FROM THE MOONSHOT MANDATE. A mega-cap at 1x will most likely produce a move of 1-3% in either direction; that is a low-variance outcome for a book whose stated purpose is asymmetric payoff. I am arguing that the highest expected return PER UNIT OF RISK today comes from owning a verified catalyst cleanly rather than owning a levered bet on a macro print, but if ORCL drifts up 3% and ORCU does 6%, the honest post-mortem is that I left half the trade on the table out of event-risk caution. I accept that trade-off and the next run should judge it as a deliberate choice, not an oversight. PRICING AND PROCEDURE, STATED PLAINLY.
